### Added
- **A remote command can hold a lock for one of its steps.** `--lock NAME` holds the name for the command's whole life, so a suite lock around `uv sync && pytest && mypy && gates` was held 20-25 minutes for a 10-minute pytest. Inside the command, `rops_lock NAME -- STEP` queues on the same machine-wide pool, holds it while STEP runs and frees it when STEP ends; `hs-rops lock status` shows the step as `<label>:step`. A name the run already holds, or a step around it, lets STEP straight through. Past the run's lock wait the step does not run (rc 75, said by name) and an `&&` chain stops there. Every run now takes its cores before its names, so a step waiting on a name never waits on a run that waits on its cores.
- **`hs-rops run --fetch PATH` brings a file the run made back with it.** A run that regenerates a tracked file on a lane (`display_catalog.py --write`) left a lane edit, and the next `run --lane` refused until a `fetch … <path> <path> --yes` was typed by hand. `--fetch` (repeatable) pulls each repo path from the run's dir to the same path here once the command ends rc 0, overwriting the copy here. A red run fetches nothing (what it left may be half-written) and prints the fetch commands; a fetch that fails makes a green run red and says the command's rc was 0. A path with no place in the repo refuses before the run, and so do `--hosts` and `--at`. The lane-edit refusal of a rebuild or a sync, and a stale-tree refusal for a path only the remote changed, now print one runnable `hs-rops fetch [--lane NAME] <path> --yes` per path, shell-quoted and capped at ten like the rows.
- **An hs-rops lane installs the node deps its lockfiles declare.** A `lane` build (and so `run --lane` that rebuilds) and `run --at` run one install per dir that holds a `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock` or `bun.lock(b)`, after the Python sync, at any depth. A lane once synced Python only, so `pnpm run typecheck` in a nested `web/` found no `node_modules` and every script carried its own install guard. A dir whose lock is unchanged since its last rc-0 install, with that install still there, is skipped; an install that failed midway vouches for nothing, so the next build installs again. A linked `node_modules` is left alone, and what an install writes beside its lock (yarn berry's state and PnP files) is the lane's own, never carried and never deleted (a zero-install repo carries the paths it commits, and only those). A tool missing on the host skips a dir `auto` found, with a note, and refuses by name, before anything installs, for a dir `ROPS_LANE_NODE` names. A failed install names its dir and quotes the cause. `ROPS_LANE_NODE` turns the steps `off` or lists the dirs (`\,` escapes a comma in a command); a dir the lane push leaves out, or a list naming none or one twice, refuses before the push; under `run --at`, a declared dir the commit predates is skipped with a note. `ROPS_LANE_SYNC_CMD` still names the Python sync alone, and the scripts runner `doctor` detects is the one whose lock the lane installs from (`bun run test`, since a bare `bun test` is bun's own test runner).
- **An hs agent runs in a session that never loaded it.** A resumed session can lose the hs plugin's agent types while their definitions sit on disk. A general-purpose spawn whose prompt opens with `hs-stand-in: <name>` and carries that agent's whole definition stands in for it: the model bound and the spawn record (and so the cook attestation) read it as `hs:<name>`. A spawn that only names the agent, or stands in for one with no model bound of its own, keeps the general-purpose cap. `hs-run cook prompt <role>` and `hs-run plan prompt <role>` print the stand-in (`stand_in`: the file, the model, the first line) beside the agent type they ask for. An Agent/Task call naming no type is read as the general-purpose agent Claude Code starts for it, so it is under that cap too (it passed the model guard unbounded); a runtime whose envelope the dispatcher translates (Grok's spawn tool arrives as `Task`) is left as it was, for the bound and the spawn record alike. Cursor's hooks carry no translation, so its envelope is read as Claude Code's and an untyped `Task` there is held to the same cap.
- **A TypeScript symbol says whether it is a React component or hook.** Both engines read one closed table (`react_rules.json`) into an optional `react` key on the symbol: role, props type, destructured keys; its kind is unchanged. `hs-code graph where --kind component|hook` lists them, and refuses by name, rather than answering zero rows, when the snapshot never computed the fact (no pack declares it for the selected engine, or the snapshot came from another harness build or another `codemap.yaml`). A file that did not parse whole carries no fact, and the answer names it rather than read as complete.
- **`test prove` and `test mutation` run a TypeScript workspace's tests in a copy.** The copy mirrors each real `node_modules` entry by entry -- also one linked out of the tree, and `.bin`/`.pnpm`/`@scope` one level deeper -- so a workspace package resolves to the copy's mutated source, a bin runs the copy's own, and a tool cache starts empty. Every run gets its own `TMPDIR` beside the copy, removed with it (not ci.sh's `/dev/shm`). The guard on the real tree also reads what the copy could write through those links; a dir too big to hash is watched by its listing only, and the run says which (`guard_entry_level`).
- **`test mutation` mutates TypeScript with the harness's own operators or the project's tool.** A language pack's `mutators:` rows: `builtin` first (byte-span operators over tree-sitter's parse, whichever engine the snapshot is measured with; a mutant that does not parse is invalid), then `stryker`, the project's own install, read back from its JSON report (a report an earlier run left is removed first, and the tool's exit is reported). A repo edits a row or adds one in `codemap.yaml`; `--mutator` picks. A file the selector reaches no test from runs its whole unit's tests and says so (`unit_fallback`); such a file that tree-sitter reads a parse error in has no valid mutant (`source_does_not_parse`, naming line:column), never a kill by an unrelated test. Under Yarn Plug'n'Play only a run of a Node tool (vitest, jest, a `kind: tool` mutator) is refused, naming Plug'n'Play: a Python probe of the same repo runs.
- **`test isolation-bisect` and `test goldens` read TypeScript.** Bisect replays a victim test file file by file, in a fresh copy per probe, through the runner's `serial:` form and the harness's own sequencer; a probe whose files did not run exactly as asked is a probe error, never a verdict. Goldens pairs a jest/vitest `.snap` under `__snapshots__/` with the test beside it, calls one whose test is gone `orphan`, and goes BLIND naming the key and file when a custom snapshot resolver is configured.
- **A register write can leave its views for later.** `glossary_register.py --add/--update` and `decision_register.py --append/--append-alloc/--amend` take `--no-render`: the YAML SSOT changes, and neither the markdown view nor the repo's declared post-write command runs, so "the SSOT moved, the view did not" can be built on purpose (a test-first docs phase watching its generated-view gate go red). `--render` / `--render-md` stay the step that brings both up. The flag on a mode that writes no SSOT is a usage error; a ledger whose markdown file is itself the SSOT refuses it, nothing written.
- **A paused phase is asked about before the plan-level review.** Once every counted phase passes and a paused phase is left, `hs-run cook next` answers `paused_remaining` (and `cook close` refuses with `phases_paused`) instead of sending the plan to a review that would judge a diff without the phase and go stale once it is built. Lift the pause to build it here, or set `closes_without: true` on the pause to close the plan without it. The automatic close at the last verify waits on the same answer, and `cook status` reports the stop at exit 0. Written one key per line, both are pause lines outside the approval hash; a flow-style `{paused: ...}` subtask is hashed whole, and `cook next` says that there either edit asks for approval again. A `closes_without` that is not a YAML bool is a lint finding. A plan already closed is not stopped.
- **A repo whose tests run on a remote host runs its harness-run tools there.** `hs-code test run` and `hs-code check run` take `--rops` (`--lane NAME`): vitest, jest, tsc and eslint run on an hs-rops lane mirroring this tree, and the verdict, the inputs digest and the ledger line are written here, as for a local run, with `where: rops:<lane>`. A lane that does not mirror the tree (checked again under the lane's lock), a run that changes the lane's tree, or a tool the lane has not installed is refused by name, and so is a tracked input of the run edited here that hs-rops never carries (`.env` at any depth, a kept data dir): the lane would read HEAD's. An untracked file there (a linked `node_modules`, IDE state) is the machine's own, and `.claude/` (the agent's session) is no input at all. The lane's scratch is removed in the background, without waiting on the lane's lock. Every command the harness routes (`hs-run cook next`, `hs-code test run --all` from a declared check, the techstack's test command) carries `--rops` where hs-rops's own configuration names a host -- a linked worktree reads the main checkout's `.rops.env`, as hs-rops does -- unless `ROPS_HS_CODE=local` keeps the tools here; the lane is `ROPS_LANE`, else the one `ROPS_REMOTE_DIR=~/rops/<name>` names, else hs-rops's own default.
- **A root nested in another on purpose says so.** `layout.roots` takes `inside: <outer id>`: the snapshot's overlap note goes quiet for that pair only, a declaration whose path no longer nests is named, and one naming no other root (or itself) is refused.
- **`hs-code init status` has an `engines` row and takes `--only`.** The row reports whether this interpreter has the Python modules each declared engine reads with, and its action is the install line itself.
- **The refactor family runs on TypeScript through the compiler.** `refactor rename`, `move --flat`, `move --symbol`, `name-repair`, `slice`, `carve` and `clone-dedupe` edit a TypeScript tree with the LanguageService of the TypeScript that lang-tools pins (never the project's `node_modules`), whichever engine reads the snapshot; without lang-tools each refuses (exit 3) with `hs-code init run --apply --only lang-tools`. A rename moves ONE declaration (several of one name: exit 3 listing them, `--in`/`--line` picks). A move across workspace packages, or of a file a package's `exports`/`main`/ `types`/`typesVersions` or a tsconfig `paths` target names (a `dist/` leaf or a `./*` pattern read through the outputs each tsconfig and its `tsconfig.<x>.json` siblings build, in place or not), is refused before it runs; an entry no build config maps back whose source is unknown -- a code file the tree does not list (a bundler's `.mjs`/`.cjs` or `kit.js` under the `outDir`, `emitDeclarationOnly`), or one it lists where a build writes (under an `outDir`, ignored yet committed, a package directory holding no project source) -- refuses every move of its own package. An asset, a path without its suffix, a `.js` entry beside its `.ts` source, a condition beside a `types` that maps back, or a committed hand-written file a build does not write (a preset, a root `main`) does not, and neither does a directory merely named `build` or `dist`. A committed build output is rebuilt, never edited; a JavaScript file's `.d.ts` moves with it, and is listed as a stale declaration when the file turns TypeScript. A JavaScript file or a shadowed `.d.ts` no tsconfig covers is read too (its imports are renamed, its tests carved); a loose script's import no tree file answers, a tracked build output of an edited source, and a code suffix in another case naming an edited file are listed as blind spots, while a loose import a tree file or a package's `exports` key answers but the service cannot resolve (a `node`/`browser`/`require` condition) refuses the run; a workspace package's stylesheet imported through `exports` is no unresolved import. Every edit is checked against each project's own program: one new error, a public specifier turned into another, or an import landing elsewhere than it did, and nothing is written. A symbol move leaves a re-export bridge recorded for `refactor shim-debt`, which reads it with the pack owning its file. Every write, the bridge ledger's included, lands inside the repo through no symlink and is all or nothing: a dry run lists what `--apply` would refuse, and a write failing midway puts back what it had written (and the `git mv`s before it). Python's verbs, payloads and exits are unchanged, except that a Python symbol move also refuses a bridge ledger reached through a symlink.
- **More hs-code verbs read TypeScript.** `change impact` (callers from the compiler's references), `change api-diff` (each workspace package's export surface with structured signatures; a breaking change suggests the bump), `check pkgsync` (each `package.json` against the imports the engine reads; laws a `package.json` gives no meaning are listed as not applicable), `scaffold new-module|new-dist` (read off the tree, `--lang` for a mixed one), `test classify|check-home|plan-move|backlog|clone-scan` (a TS test file is one file-level item, homed beside its unit) and the `graph rules` kinds `code_shape`, `dup_symbol`, `file_size`, `landfall`, `single_door`, `pkg_door` (a cause with no meaning in TypeScript says why; `packaging` reads `not_applicable`); `map` reads every language, its default include the globs of the packs the snapshot holds.
- **What a language serves is data.** A verb serves a language only when its registry row (`languages:`) and the pack's `verbs:` row in `harness/data/hs-code-languages.yaml` both say so; a rule kind by the pack's `kinds:`. The book also names a pack's reader for `graph importers --symbol` (`symbol_uses`, gated by the `importers_symbol` capability), its `test mutation` entry, the first summary keys a mutator row keeps (`summary_schema`), and the suffixes a TypeScript reader takes come from the pack's `files.include`. No codegraph code compares a language id outside 16 reasoned sites.

- **`hs-rops` waits for seats as long as the call asks.** `run`, every `ROPS_CMD_*` alias, `lane`, `sync`, `bench` and `ci run` take `--lock-wait S`: how long the run waits for all of its seats (lane dir, `--lock`, env locks, cpu) before it gives up with rc 75 and nothing run, over `ROPS_LOCK_WAIT` for that call. Every pool shares one deadline, read once on the far side: a wait per pool let a run behind two busy pools wait twice as long, past the client's ssh cut, and run after the client had left. With neither, the wait is 1800s, or a typed longer `--timeout` (`--timeout 3000` gave up at 1800s), and never past the call's `--timeout` less a margin, typed or the verb's default (`run`'s own 1800s waited 1800s, so a busy queue read 124, never 75): the margin lets the give-up reach the caller as rc 75 before ssh cuts the call. It is a quarter of the timeout, 5s at least and 60s at most (`--timeout 60` waits 45s, not 1s; `--timeout 300` 240s; `--timeout 1860` 1800s), and a lane rebuilt for the run waits for its dir as long. A named wait is kept; one reaching within the margin of the timeout is said once on stderr, as reading 124, detached. A wait that is not a positive whole number of seconds, or is longer than 7 days, is refused by name, also from `ROPS_LOCK_WAIT` (it crashed in `int()`, and past 2147483 s in `OverflowError`); the give-up line names the flag and the verbs that take it. hs-code's lane runs name a 1800s wait, so their rc 75 comes back inside their own `--timeout`. hs-rops flags take no abbreviation: `--lock-wait` made `--loc` ambiguous, and an alias handed it to the command with no lock held.
### Changed
- **17 verb rows leave a language out for good, and say why.** On TypeScript: `refactor slice-audit|repin-hash|rebind|rewrite-refs`, `test fixture-shadow`, `check f821|smoke|route-parity|live-smoke` and the 7 `port` verbs; on Python: `check run`. Each refuses (exit 3) with its `language_reason`, never as "not yet". A row leaving out a language with no reason is a test failure.
- **The language gate refuses what it let through.** `refactor rename` with no target no longer scans only `*.py` and answers "occurs nowhere" on a TypeScript tree, and a TypeScript file in a repo whose `codemap.yaml` does not declare `typescript` is refused by name instead of being read as Python. `test classify` and `test check-home` now declare `languages: [python, typescript]`, so a repo with a project language (`adapters:` + `resolver:`) sees them refuse or warn `languages_not_considered` for it.
- **`change api-diff` from a snapshot on a mixed repo** compares the Python surface and lists the TypeScript one as not compared; TypeScript alone refuses (exit 3).
- **`hs-rops fetch` takes several lane paths, each brought to its own path here; `--to DEST` names a destination.** Two relative paths were read as `SRC DEST`, so a second lane path became the destination: `fetch --lane L erd-7.svg 05-4.md --yes` wrote the SVG over a tracked `.md`. Now every relative path is a lane file landing at the same path in this repo, checked to exist there and to be overwritable before anything is copied. `SRC DEST` stays only where one side is absolute or `~` (no place in this tree), and there an existing file of another suffix is not overwritten even with `--yes`. Two relative paths where the second is not in this tree read both ways and are refused, printing both commands. Printed commands carry `--host`/`--lane`, quote each word and put paths after `--`; the suite chain and the verification hint name their local file with `--to`.
- **`hs-code test run`: a test file that does not load is a FAIL naming it, not BLOCKED.** vitest and jest report such a file with no assertions; the run now names it and fails, and a failed assertion in another file still counts beside it. So does a test file a hook failed outside any test (vitest's `beforeAll` skips its block's tests, an `afterAll` leaves them passed: the file fails, the counts read 0 failed); its JUnit carries an `(outside tests)` error case.
- **The language book is parsed once per version of its file.** The shell asked the book for every argument and test function, and each call re-parsed the YAML; the parse is cached on the file's path, mtime, size and inode, so an edited book is read again.

### Fixed
- **Two runs on one hs-rops lane never rebuild it at once.** A wait for the lane dir held nothing: two runs found it free, both rebuilt it, and one `rsync --delete` ran under the other (rc 24, the command never ran). The wait now holds the dir's seat; the build's steps ride on it and the command takes it over in the same mutex hold. A run that queued skips the rebuild when the lane it finds is already this tree with its build finished.
- **The spawn nudge reads usage under a time budget.** It re-read every transcript ever written on each Agent call (4 GB here, ~30-50 s) and the dispatcher killed it at 5 s, so every spawn paid 5 s and the reminder never showed. The meter skips transcripts untouched since the longest window opened, keeps a per-file ledger of the offset read, and the hook bounds a read at 2.5 s, answering a lower bound (`note`) the next spawn completes.
- **Two clones of one commit read the same ignore rules.** The code map's ignore reads obeyed the operator's `core.excludesFile` and a clone's own exclude, so one tree read as built on one machine and hand-written on another. Only the tree's `.gitignore` files count.
- **An hs-family command on a merged stream still prints one envelope.** With stderr into the same pipe or file as stdout (`2>&1`), the human summary and a refusal's repeat landed after the JSON line and `json.load` failed ("Extra data"). On a merged stream the repeats are left out and other stderr rides in `warnings`.
- **`gate_stage` judges a spelled-out write target under a plan's artifacts dir by the file it names.** A heredoc writing a runner script there was refused as forgery. A redirect, `tee` or `dd` target spelled out whole is resolved and refused only when it names what the cage holds; one with an expansion, glob, escape or quote is still refused. A heredoc whose opener redirects into `verification.json` slipped past the heredoc strip; it no longer does.
- **A Playwright spec beside a vitest config is not an unowned file.** The TypeScript pack declares Playwright as an agent-run e2e runner (`executor: agent`), set up by its config. A file a harness runner's list step leaves out goes to it only when Playwright's own list step (`test --list --reporter=json`) names the file; the rest stay unowned. A check that ran nothing of its own is SKIP.
- **What makes a TypeScript package one that builds is the pack's table.** `languageservice.build_signals` (script keys read word by word, config files at the package root, `package.json` keys a bundler reads, Nx/moon/Turborepo build targets, `own_only` rows) and `entry_fields` replace hand-coded guesses; a package builds when it or a package above it up to the workspace root matches a row. A build tool missing there reads as hand-written: add its row.
- **An `ask_user` option YAML reads as a mapping reaches the gate as one.** Two cook options holding an unquoted `closes_without: true` printed a dict; the gate now names such an option, and the two are quoted.
- **A non-UTF-8 tracked path does not stop the plan's evidence scan.**
- **A dependency spliced into an empty `package.json` is valid JSON.**
- **hs-rops walks a lane path physically.** zsh's `cd` reads `..` by the letter, so a lane reached through a symlink was no lane to the guard while rsync landed in it. A middle-slash exclude (`a/b/`) is matched at any depth, as rsync does.
- **`hs-code test run` says how many tests ran.** Each check carries `tests`: how many ran, failed and were skipped, summed over its units' result files, and the text view prints them beside the status. `PASS` alone read the same for a run of 3 tests and one of 3000.
- **`cook verify` in the checkout a lane merged into records the lane's work.** A phase opened and committed in a linked worktree, merged `--no-ff` here, was refused (exit 3) as "no commit in <here> ... but <lane> opened it and holds ..." though every one of its commits was in HEAD's history. When one tree holds the phase's work and all of the set it computes has merged here, that set is recorded, with a warning naming the tree; two such trees, or work not yet merged, still refuse. When the tree that opened the phase is gone, the verify records as before but names the commits merged since its mark that no other phase recorded, and how to record them.
- **The fetch commands an hs-rops refusal prints lose nothing here.** A lane-edit refusal printed `fetch … <path> --yes` for a path this tree had edited too, and running it overwrote the uncommitted edit. Only a path this tree leaves at HEAD gets `--yes`; one edited on both sides is fetched beside the copy here as `<path>.lane`. "Edited here" is read off the bytes on disk, so a file ignored here (`.git/info/exclude`, `core.excludesFile`) whose bytes differ from what rops last wrote there, or from HEAD's, counts too, with no `--yes`, and the refusal says to compare the two. Every printed fetch names the host and lane the run used and puts `--` before the path (`-x.json` read as a flag); a path that is not UTF-8 gets a note, not a command that fetches another file. `run --fetch` after rc 75 (the queue gave up) says so and prints none. The refusal also says a file only the lane needs can live in `$TMPDIR` and be fetched by absolute path.
- **An hs-rops run whose last pytest summary ran no test is red.** `no tests ran`, every test deselected, or only skips read green under rc 0; such a closing line now reports 1 and says so. The files-only exemption now follows every program the command reaches, inside `$(...)`, backticks and `bash -c '...'`: `echo "$(pytest)"` is read, `bash -c 'cat log'` is not, and `cat log | python3 x.py` is read (python3 can run anything; `ROPS_SUMMARY_CHECK=off` for such a run). `awk` and `sed` count as readers only when their script can run nothing: awk without `system`, `getline`, a pipe or a redirect, sed without an `e` command or flag and without `w`/`W`; `$((...))` is arithmetic, not a command. A `--collect-only` closing line (`9/10 tests collected (1 deselected)`) runs none on purpose and is never red.
- **An `ROPS_ENV_CHECK` that answers 124 or 255 itself is a refusal, not a cut or an ssh failure.** The far side prints the check's own rc on a line of its own after the check's group ends, with a token fresh per call; the last such line is read, so a background job printing after the check, or a marker the check prints itself, changes nothing. With that line back, any nonzero is "not there" with its rc; without it 124 is the cut, 255 ssh, and anything else fails closed as broken (exit 2) with the last output lines, never a pass. What the check printed is masked like the command: a `password=`, `token=`, `secret=` (in a DSN or a query string) and a `PGPASSWORD=` it echoed are `***`. A printed command masks every leading `NAME=value` whatever its name (`REDIS_PW=x cmd`, `export X=`, `env X=`); inside arguments only a secret-looking name or a declared value is masked, so `-o BatchMode=yes` reads as written.
- **An hs-rops run whose log closes on a red pytest summary is red.** The rc is the command's last statement's, so `pytest … | tail -60; echo "rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"` came back `exit_code 0` with pytest rc 1 and `rc=1` in the log. A run that exits 0 while the last summary line in its full log names a failure or an error now reports 1, and a `!! ` line says why. Only the last summary counts (a rerun that went green stays green), any command shape is read, and a command that only prints files back (`cat`, `grep`, `tail`) is not. `ROPS_SUMMARY_CHECK=off` turns it off.
- **`hs-rops fetch` with no dest puts the file at its own path in this repo.** It wrote the basename into the current dir: `fetch --lane L packages/x/display-catalog.json` landed beside the tree, and the file it was meant to replace stayed as it was. A relative path now lands at the same path under the repo (a lane and `ROPS_REMOTE_DIR` mirror the tree), wherever the shell stands; one that leaves the repo (`..`) is refused, and so is an absolute or `~` path with no dest, each naming the `fetch <path> <dest>` form. `--yes` still decides an overwrite.
- **`cook verify` refuses when its tree holds none of the phase's work but another tree holds some.** A phase can be opened and built in a linked worktree, then verified from the main checkout. The main tree's own mark had nothing after it, so the verify used to record an empty commit range without a word, and a later `--sha keep` refused because that record named no commit. It now exits 3, records nothing, and names the tree that holds the work and its commits. It gives the two ways on: verify there, or name the commits here with `--sha`.
- **`hs-rops` rebuilds a lane whose last build did not finish.** A lane build removes its record first and writes it last. A step that failed after the tree moved left a lane with no record, and `run --sync` read that tree as current and ran in a lane with no venv. That lane is now rebuilt. The sync, editable-repair and setup steps run in the lane being built. They used to run in the checkout's own remote dir, and when the two differed their `cd` was the first thing to fail.
- **A `hs-rops` core-pool ledger swept from the host's temp dir is made again under a waiting run.** Each ledger entry recreates the dir. An `epoch` file written with the dir tells a waiting run that its ticket went with the sweep, not with a cancel, so it puts the ticket back and keeps its place.
- **`cook verify` on a phase nothing ever opened refuses rather than record no commit.** A phase built while its prerequisite still waited for its verify gets no open mark, because no `cook next` ever projected it. Its verify used to set the mark at HEAD and record an empty commit set, with the commits since the prerequisite's last verify only in a warning; the agent then re-verified with them by hand. Now, when such commits exist, it exits 3, records nothing, and prints the ready `--sha` line. To take the empty record on purpose, open the phase first (`cook next`) and verify again. A commit that another phase's latest verify recorded is that phase's, so it is no longer offered. With nothing since, the old warning and the empty record stay.
- **`hs-rops` refuses a run whose `ROPS_ENV` names something that is not there.** A repo declares `ROPS_ENV_CHECK`, a command that fails while the resource is missing. It runs in the run's dir with `ROPS_ENV` exported, before every `run`, `ROPS_CMD_*` alias, `--at` and fan-out command. When it fails, the command does not run: exit 3, with the check, its rc, its last output lines, the env names and the lane, and the fix (declare `ROPS_LANE_SETUP`, then `hs-rops lane`). Env values are never printed, as written or as the far shell exported them; every `secret_patterns` shape, any `scheme://<credential>@` (an empty user, a token as the user) and a command's leading `NAME=value` are masked, the same in `doctor`, which runs the check as `env check`. A check cut at its 120s (exit 124) or never reached over ssh (exit 2) says so and is no refusal: it names no setup for an env nobody checked. When a `{lane}`/`{lane_id}` value has neither `ROPS_LANE_SETUP` nor `ROPS_ENV_CHECK`, `lane` and `doctor` warn. Before this, a lane whose database `vsf_{lane_id}` was never created ran its suite anyway: 189 skips, ~29 `PoolTimeout` failures, and no line named the database.
- **`hs-rops` never exports one lane's `ROPS_ENV` into another lane.** A `.rops.env` (or the environment) that declares `ROPS_LANE` beside `ROPS_ENV` now binds that env to its lane. A run in a different lane refuses with exit 3 before it touches anything: `run --lane X`, the main checkout's file read from a linked worktree, `lane` building another lane, and fan-out. The refusal names the file, its lane and the run's lane. Before this, `run --lane intake2-65a` from a worktree moved only the lane dir and kept the main checkout's `VSF_DATABASE_URL=…/vsf_b2_main`, so the suite truncated another lane's database. A value can write the lane into itself, `{lane}` verbatim or `{lane_id}` (made safe for a database name). Such a value follows every run's lane. `doctor` prints the lane each `ROPS_ENV` was declared for and fails on a mismatch.
- **`verify_install` (and `hs-cli doctor`) names a wired plugin that cannot load.** A project settings file can enable `hs@hs-local` and still load nothing: the directory marketplace it names holds no `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` of that name declaring the plugin (a dev farm is no marketplace), Claude Code does not know the marketplace, or its install ledger holds no install of the plugin for this project (an update can leave only another project's). Each is a warning naming the file and the command that repairs it; `--strict` stays green, as for every per-machine check.
- **A transcript or ledger record holding U+2028, U+2029 or U+0085 is read whole.** `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)` leaves those three raw inside a string, and `str.splitlines()` cut the record there, so both halves failed to parse: the open-question finder, the subagent outcome, the session summary and the spawn ledger lost it, and the ledger's trim wrote the two halves back as two broken lines. Every reader of a JSON-lines text a `str` writer wrote now cuts at `"\n"` alone (`text_lines.py`): the run ledger and its trim, the trace chain verifier and the day checkpoint's record count (a record holding one failed the chain), the trace tail the prompt nudges read, the dismissals, decision, port, shadow, consent, autonomy and telemetry ledgers, and the touched-path flags of the standards-drift and memory-gap nudges. A test keeps on it every `splitlines()`, whatever its arguments, in a function that parses JSON or in a same-file helper such a function calls; each exempt site is named by its function, and reads bytes, a command's output, source text or a plain-text file.
- **An advisory agent is blamed only for a file its own calls write.** Every hook attachment in a transcript carries the hook's command line, so `hook_dispatch.py` was named in every agent's transcript, and a change another session landed while the agent ran was reported as the agent's mutation. A changed file is now the agent's when one of its calls writes or removes it: the target of Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit, of a Bash command (read the way the write guard reads one, `cd`s and the record's own working directory included) or of a write-shaped MCP tool. A file tool's path is matched as written; a shell word as written or as the shell expands it; what `rm`, `mv`, `git rm` or a copy reaches, with everything beneath it, whether or not the directory still exists when the agent stops; a git pathspec the way git matches it (`'h/*.py'` reaches `h/x/f.py`); the whole worktree under `git stash`, `reset --hard`, a forced checkout, a branch switch or `git apply`; what `patch` writes under its `-d` directory, or its file operand; and what a `find` deletes or hands to a writing `-exec`, by its `-name`. `git clean` never removes a tracked file and is not counted. A shell line is read only when one of its words names a changed file or a directory above one. Each `cd` is read as succeeding, so a mutation proof that restores a file inside a scratch copy is no longer the agent's write to the repo. A file its calls only name (a read, a `sed -n`) is reported apart, as read or written some way no call shows or changed by another session; one it never names is reported as another session's change or a write of the agent's that names no file. A fault while reading the transcript reports every change as the agent's, as before.
- **A search for the words `sed -i` writes nothing.** The shell write reader took every word of any command holding `sed -i` as a write target, so `grep -n "sed -i" f` wrote `f`. grep, rg (without `--pre`), echo and printf (without `-v`), called by their bare name with no wrapper or assignment ahead of it, only print their words, so they are let off when nothing on the line hands that output on (no pipe, redirect, command or process substitution or `coproc`) and nothing on it may change what the name runs (no function or alias by that name or `sed`'s, no `PATH` change, no `hash`, `enable`, `builtin` or `command`). Every other command holding `sed -i` still reads as writing all its words: a wrapper the reader does not know (`flock l sed -i f`) runs it, any `sed` may run a shell through its `e` command, and a shell may read a printed line (`echo 'sed -i s/a/b/ f' | sh`).
- **An evidence path a plan document writes from its own directory resolves.** A research note citing `probes/setup.sh` meant the `probes/` beside it, the way a markdown link in that note resolves, but the evidence check tried only the repo root and the plan dir, and blocked cook on a file that was there. The citing document's own directory is tried too, still never reaching out of the repo.
- **An unattested subagent record names the hold that changes no plan file first.** The warning after `cook record developer` used to offer only `posture: in_place` in plan.md's frontmatter — a file the approval pins, so following it re-opened approval on every phase. It now names `hs-run cook prompt developer --phase P --flags in_place` first, and says the frontmatter route means approving the plan again. A plan that itself declares `posture: subagent` is told only the frontmatter route: `--flags in_place` against it is a refused conflict.
- **A lane rebuild no longer throws away, unasked, what was written on the lane.** `run --lane N --stale-ok` rebuilt a mismatched lane anyway, and the reset took six tapes a run had just recorded there, with no word of it. `--stale-ok` now runs on the lane as it is. A build records what the lane holds when it is done; the next rebuild refuses with rc 3, before anything is pushed or reset, over a path changed there since that it would destroy -- a tracked edit anywhere (excluded paths too: `reset --hard` reaches them), an unignored new file, a commit -- names each, and points at `fetch --lane`. `--discard-lane-edits` or `ROPS_LANE_EDITS=discard` rebuilds over them and lists them. Ignored files and `plans/` stay the rebuild's to remove (a kept name keeps an output). `sync` onto a lane, however its path is spelled (`~/rops/N`, relative to the home, absolute, through a symlink -- its last component's too -- or a `..`; `$HOME`, which rsync takes literally, is refused before anything is made), waits out a run holding the lane (taking no `ROPS_LOCK_ENV` seat) and runs the same check over what it would overwrite -- still against the record after a commit on the lane or a HEAD moved back there; a commit it never moves and the next rebuild still names -- and keeps the record true, however many paths it lists. A lane that cannot be read, or a path the host cannot place, refuses; `--sync --stale-ok` is refused.
- **A global install with no `HARNESS_DATA_ROOT` writes the plan of the project it stands in.** `write_review_decision`, `plan_approval`, `cook close`, `hs-run plan record` and `backlog_register` refused (`zone 'plans' needs a project root but none resolved`) while `cook record` in the same chain walked up to the plan's `plans/` and wrote. The guard now takes the project the tool found walking up from its cwd, when the environment names none and it is neither the shared bin nor `/`. A `HARNESS_DATA_ROOT` that is set but wrong stays a refusal.
- **A phase verified in a linked worktree records its blast radius.** The record decided "code change or not" from the tree's own diff, empty on a lane branch with no upstream and a clean tree, and wrote no `blastRadius` key at all. The files the phase's commits touched now count too, and a derivation that fails says so in the key.
- **Re-verifying a phase after the next one opened keeps the next one's commits out.** The range ran from the phase's mark to HEAD; it now stops at the first open mark of a phase opened in the same tree after this one was verified (a later claim of a phase opened earlier is no new open), and the warning lists the commits left out with this phase's own `--sha` set to add one to.
- **`hs-rops run --lane` carries a new host plan file to a lane at the same HEAD.** The host checkout's `plans/` reached the lane only on a rebuild. A run with nothing new in `plans/` writes nothing; a change waits on the lane's lock first.
- **Two remote runs by one user can keep out of each other's temp dirs.** `ROPS_RUN_TMPDIR=on` exports a `TMPDIR` of its own under the host's for every `hs-rops run` and removes it when the run's shell exits. Off by default: a command that sets its own `TMPDIR` (a `ci.sh` picking `/dev/shm`, with its own free-space floor) would lose it. A red run whose log says `could not create numbered dir` (a pytest basetemp lost to a run beside it: 159 errors) now names the key, and `--basetemp`, to fix it.
- **A pytest run whose log holds no summary line is red.** `hs-rops test` (and any `hs-rops run` whose pytest prints into the log) ended `exit_code=0` on a log of app start-up output with no `collected`/`passed` line, which read as green. One pytest printing into the log (`[cd/export … &&] pytest … [| tail/tee]`) now owes it a summary line; none, and the run says `no pytest summary in the log` and returns 1. A shape the check cannot read for sure (`;`, `||`, a group, `bash -c`, output sent elsewhere) owes none, nor do `-qq`, `-p no:terminal`, `--version` or a timed-out run; `ROPS_SUMMARY_CHECK=off` turns it off.
- **A lane whose dependency sync fails names the step and its cause.** `uv sync --frozen` refusing a stale `uv.lock` came back as `bringing lane up ended rc=2` alone; the build now prints `step 5, dependency sync` with the tool's `error:`/`hint:`/ `ERROR:`/`npm ERR!` lines (uv's `To update the lockfile, run uv lock`), or the log's path when it has none.
- **A remote run's log keeps the stop line written into it.** The run's output was opened over the file, so a shell outliving its stopped child wrote over the reaper's line that said who stopped it.
- **hs-rops no longer deletes a lane's linked install.** A `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.venv-ci` that is a symlink on the lane matched no directory-only exclude, so every push removed it as a stray, and it counted toward the lane's fingerprint, so the lane never read `== local` again. Only these install names get the slash-less twin, in the push and the fingerprint alike: another kept name (`logs`) stays a directory pattern, so a tracked file of that name (`bin/logs`) is still carried.
- **The two TypeScript engines are always compared.** The comparison test waited on the other engine's tests, and an order that ran it first skipped it every time.
- **A stale code fact the snapshot cannot refresh says what to install.** `cook next` handed over `hs-code graph snapshot` (exit 11) where the codemap's engine had no modules in this interpreter, the step was refused, and the next `cook next` moved on to review. It is now `facts_stale` at exit 10, naming the missing modules and their install line -- or exit 11 with `hs-code init run --apply --only lang-tools` first, where only a row `init run` sets up is missing. The question is asked of the `hs-code` launcher, the interpreter the refresh runs under; `init run --apply` exits 1 while a row it cannot set up (`engines`) is unready, instead of reporting done.
- **Under a `uv run` interpreter the install hint is the whole `HARNESS_PYTHON` line**, with `--with` right after `uv run`, where uv reads it (after the command it is handed to the command).
- **A lane verify reads the blast radius from the tree holding the phase's commits** (`--tree`), not from the checkout holding the plan -- also before the phase's first commit; a `--tree` that is no git checkout is refused instead of dropped.
- **A root at `path: .` is the outer of every other root.** The overlap note never named a root nested under it, and `inside: <that id>` was reported as not nesting.
- **A dead evidence citation written from a package root names the file it means.** When a cited path is not at the repo root but exactly one tracked file ends with it (`tests_repo/worker/t.py` inside `packages/gates/`), the preflight finding says "did you mean `<full path>`"; two or more are counted, never guessed. Every dead citation is still reported in one pass.
- **hs-rops names a mid-merge index instead of advising `--sync`.** With conflict stages in the local index, a lane can never read equal (it mirrors stage 0 only), and the refusal said "add --sync" even to a run that had it. It now names the unmerged paths and says to resolve and `git add` them; after a `--lane` rebuild, what still differs is never advice to sync again.
- **A lane mirrors an intent-to-add entry (`git add -N`).** It sits in the index with no content staged, so the mirror -- reading `diff --cached` -- left it out, the lane listed one path less, and every `run --lane --sync` refused with `different index` and advice to add the `--sync` it already had.
- **A command of unknown width says it holds the whole cpu pool and how to ask less.** It printed `asks 100000`, an internal number, and the `--cores 1` hint only once it queued; the line now names the pool's seats and the hint is said at once, and once.
- **A TypeScript engine is never chosen for the project past the load.** The resolver's configs, the tsconfig files a check or test run's digest reads, and `graph importers --symbol` fell back to tree-sitter when a descriptor carried no `languages.typescript.engine` -- the digest even under `engine: typescript`, so a tsconfig only the compiler resolves could be edited without staling a PASS. They now ask one function, which names the missing key, and the tsconfig and tree readers have no engine of their own to fall back on. A `codemap.yaml` load already refused it.
- **The register's block names `--amend` beside `--append`.** Fixing a live ruling's text or anchors spends no new id; the write guard's route line said only `--append`.
- **A release cut bumps, and commits, the docs that version with the kit.** Three cuts in a row (7.1.0, 7.2.0, 7.3.0) pinned `harness/release.json` and left every kit-versioned doc at the previous number, so the next commit went red and the docs were bumped by hand. `release.py --apply` now bumps each listed doc's frontmatter `version` before writing anything else, and stops the cut when one has none. Both doors that commit a cut -- `release.py --push` and the `hs:release` engine -- stage one list (`cut_files`), so the bumped docs land in the release commit instead of being left dirty after it.
- **The dev skill farm loads under Claude Code 2.1.306.** That release reads no plugin file a symlink resolves to outside the plugin and marketplace directories, and every farm entry links into `harness/plugins`, so a marketplace rooted at the farm loaded nothing: every hs skill and agent vanished from new sessions. `dev_skill_farm.py --build` writes the marketplace manifest at the repo root, where both ends of each link sit inside it, and `--check` refuses a missing or stale manifest and any farm link that escapes the root.
